## Intent
Hypothesis: Halide code generation for walk1 can auto-vectorize per-particle math to approach the streaming ceiling, with the simple host-scan walk2 adding only modest overhead.

## Cache saturation
The L1d spill at N≈949 falls below the smallest measured point (N=4000), so that transition is unobserved. At N=4000 (276 KB, within L2), cost is high—10.888 ns/p at q=0.01—reflecting unamortized setup overhead. Cost FALLS sharply to N=65000 (10.888→6.583 ns/p) as per-particle overhead amortizes. The L2 spill at N≈60787 sits just below N=65000; crossing into DRAM produces no knee—cost rises only gently to 6.88 ns/p at N=4000000. Death rate raises the floor without changing the N-shape: at q=0.25 the curve floors at ~8.4 ns/p versus ~6.6, with slightly steeper large-N degradation (8.425→8.885).

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 10.48 GB/s at N=65000, q=0.01—42% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling. Overhead-bound at small N (6.34 GB/s at N=4000), the algo reaches a compute/branch-bound plateau by N=65000 where bandwidth stalls near 10 GB/s rather than climbing toward ceiling. Bandwidth slightly declines at larger N (10.48→10.03, N=65000→4000000), confirming it is not streaming-limited. Death rate erodes the plateau: peak falls from 10.48 GB/s (q=0.01) to 8.19 GB/s (q=0.25, 33% of ceiling) as the branchy spawn loop fires more often.

## Assembly
The host code is entirely scalar—0 vector-suffixed instructions. The per-particle update loop (0x10005ade0) uses `ldp s5, s6`, `fadd s5`, `fmul s5`, `fcvtzs`, with byte-granular `strb` scatter stores. The only SIMD is the walk2 mask-scan fast path (0x10005b04c): `ldp q1, q0` loads 32 mask bytes, `orr.16b` + `ext.16b` + `orr.8b` reduce them to skip empty chunks. Walk1 is offloaded to `bl _halide_b3_mask`; its internals are not in evidence, so whether Halide vectorized walk1 cannot be determined. The 34 `bl` calls to `spawn` and scalar byte stores explain the 42% ceiling.

## Verdict
Partially holds—at q=0.01 the algo sustains 10.48 GB/s (42% of ceiling) at N=65000 with no L2-spill knee, confirming overhead amortizes and the mask-scan skips empty regions. But approaching the streaming ceiling is refuted: host-side per-particle math is entirely scalar and scatter uses byte-granular `strb` stores, capping bandwidth at 42% regardless of N. At q=0.25 the branchy spawn loop erodes the plateau to 8.19 GB/s (33% of ceiling), so the hypothesis holds only in the low-churn regime and well below ceiling.
